entry.title: Victim, driver identified in fatal car vs pedestrian at 9th and Grace
entry.content:
From useful.bike

From the Richmond Police:

Pedestrian Identified, Driver Charged in Fatal Collision Last Week on North 9th Street

Richmond Police investigators have identified the pedestrian who was fatally struck on North 9th Street last Friday and have charged the driver involved.

On Friday at approximately 5:42 p.m., officers were called to the intersection of East Grace and North 9th streets for the report of a vehicle striking a pedestrian.

Officers arrived and found an adult male, identified as Joseph Vass, Jr., 98, of Quinton, VA, down and injured in the roadway of North 9th Street. He had been struck in the intersection while riding a mobility scooter. He was transported to a local hospital where he succumbed to his injuries later that evening.

The driver of the striking vehicle stayed on the scene and reported he was turning left from East Grace Street onto North 9th Street when he struck Vass on his scooter. The driver, Nicholas Gurick, Jr., 79, of Chesterfield County, surrendered to the Richmond Justice Center yesterday and has been charged with failure to stop for a pedestrian in a crosswalk resulting in death.

Anyone with further information is asked to call RPD Crash Team Investigator T. Harrell at (804) 709-4057 or call Crime Stoppers at (804) 780-1000. The P3 Tips Crime Stoppers app for smartphones also may be used. All Crime Stoppers reporting methods are anonymous.

entry.title: Leigh Street slated for sidewalk improvements, shared use path
entry.content:
From useful.bike

The Biotech Phase III – Leigh Street Streetscape Project will provide signal improvements at the intersections, sidewalk installation, a shared use path, and streetscape improvements along Leigh Street from 4th Street to the Martin Luther King Bridge.

The $7,103,000 project appears to be fully funded and was initially slated to start this past summer.

The improvements will stretch almost 10 blocks. The projects connects on the east end to the bike lanes on the MLK Bridge, and will stop 3 blocks short of the 1st Street bike lanes (and proposed route of the Fall Line Trail through the city).

entry.title: Imagine a shared use path along Huguenot from the James River to Pocahontas Park
entry.content:
From useful.bike

One day we could have some sort of bike way along Huguenot Road, but probably not anytime soon.

The City of Richmond’s 2024 Richmond Connects Strategic Plan (“A Multimodal Plan for Improving Transportation Equity in Richmond”)(PDF) lists the possible “Huguenot Road Bikeway” as a “Priority Project” but of “secondary” (vs primary) relevance. The project seems to be at the “sure would be nice” phase, which is a very long way from an actual rideable piece of infrastructure.

The scope of the project is the stretch of Huguenot Road from the Chippenham overpass north to the bridge over the James River. The roadway is currently two travel lanes in each direction, with a turn lane on the center of the road. There is no sidewalk on either side. Traffic through the area at max use is a hectic and aggressive bad experience as a driver and is super sketchy on a bike.

Huguenot Road just south of the bridge (via Google Streetview)

The Richmond Connects Strategic Plan describes two potential approaches to making the corridor less of a Mad Max experience - a shared use path or converting one lane of vehicular traffic in each direction into bike lanes. Next steps would be to determine feasibility of the designs and then running them by the community - but there doesn’t appear to be any movement on this.

North of the bridge, River Road and Cary Street Road are decidedly not bike friendly, though the University of Richmond’s Eco Corridor Trail is a great connector out of this area into safer neighborhood streets.

South of the Chippenham overpass, Huguenot Road enters Chesterfield County. The county’s 2015 Bikeways Plan (PDF) shows a proposed bikeway/trail “on or along the road” here. The draft of the county’s new Active Transportation Plan proposes a shared use path along Huguenot from the Chippenham overpass south all the way to Pocahontas Park.

From the draft of Chesterfield County’s Active Transportation Plan

entry.title: Victim identified, arrest made in today’s fatal hit and run
entry.content:
From useful.bike

From Richmond Police Department:

Victim Identified, Arrest Made in Fatal Hit and Run Involving Pedestrian on East Main Street

Richmond Police Department investigators have identified the pedestrian who was fatally struck on East Main Street today and have arrested the driver involved.

At approximately 10:17 a.m., officers were called to the intersection of East Main and 21st streets for the report of a hit and run involving a pedestrian.

Officers arrived and found an adult male, identified as Harry Laverty, 75, of Richmond, down and unresponsive in the roadway of East Main Street. He was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.

The driver of the striking vehicle had left the scene prior to the arrival of officers. The Richmond Police Department Crash Team responded to investigate. Crash Team investigators collected video from nearby businesses and used other investigative techniques to identify the vehicle and driver.

Investigators arrested John Mcsparren, 47, of North Chesterfield, and charged him with felony hit and run. His booking photo is not yet available.

RPD thanks all those who came forward with information regarding this tragic collision which assisted investigators.

Anyone with further information is asked to call RPD Crash Team Investigator T. Harrell at (804) 709-4057 or call Crime Stoppers at (804) 780-1000. The P3 Tips Crime Stoppers app for smartphones also may be used. All Crime Stoppers reporting methods are anonymous.

entry.title: What’s Happening in November at the Main Library!
entry.content:
From r/rva

Events taking place at Richmond Public Library’s Main Library (101 E. Franklin St.) during the month of November 2026!

FIRST FRIDAY & FRIENDS OF THE LIBRARY BOOK SALE

Friday, November 6th, all evening!

We will have a First Friday Gallery Opening event and the Book Sale will be happening at the same time! Join the Friends of Richmond Public Library for their Fall Book Sale. Bring a bag and pick up some great deals on books, CDs, DVDs, and more.

The Fall Book Sale Hours are as follows:

  • Friday, Nov. 6, 10:00 AM-12:00 PM (Members Only)
  • Friday, Nov. 6, 12:00-8:00 PM
  • Saturday, Nov. 7, 10:00 AM-4:00 PM
  • Sunday, Nov. 8, 1:00-4:00 PM

Proceeds from the Book Sale benefit Richmond Public Library programming. Visit https://rvalibraryfriends.org/ to learn more about the Friends or to sign up to become a member.

FALL CONCERT SERIES: ALAN BILLER X SARA BOUCHARD

Saturday, November 7th from 2:00 PM – 3:00 PM

Sara Bouchard is a multidisciplinary artist and composer who uses sound, installation, works on paper, performance and creative coding to interweave song, history and the landscape. She is currently based in Richmond, VA, where she teaches at Virginia Commonwealth University School of the Arts.

Guitarist Alan Biller has lived and performed in NYC, Montreal, Washington DC, and Richmond, VA as part of their lively jazz scenes. He has performed worldwide with the Capital Focus Jazz Band, playing at the French Quarter Festival in New Orleans, the Old Sacramento Dixieland Jazz Jubilee, and the Ascona Jazz Festival in Ascona, Switzerland. He also spent several months performing on Carnival Cruise Lines and lived to tell about it. He has studied with such famous (and infamous) jazz greats as Bruce Arnold, Mordy Ferber, Ron McClure, Frank Kimbrough, and George Garzone. He received his BMus from NYU. With his solo project Wolf In Wool, he tries to make his guitar sound like anything but a guitar, with varying levels of success.

EXPLORING ADOPTION, IDENTITY & BELONGING DURING NATIONAL ADOPTION AWARENESS MONTH

Mondays in November at 1:00 PM

Educational sessions with experts from C2Adopt that helps the public understand the realities of foster care, waiting children, kinship care, and the need for permanent families for Virginia’s children. This session includes exploring myth vs. fact; how to become a foster or adoptive parent; spotlight on older youth and sibling groups; and other ways to support even if parenting is not for you.

Week 1 — Understanding Foster Care, Kinship Care & Adoption Today

Week 2 — “Whose Story Is It?” — Identity, Records & the Lifelong Impact of Adoption

Week 3 — Talking About Adoption with Children: Building Healthy Family Narratives

Week 4 — Adoption Through the Lifespan: Voices of Experience

DR. HILARY LEVINSON ON TRANSLATION

Sunday, November 8th, 2:00 PM – 3:30 PM

Dr. Hilary Levinson will give a talk discussing scholarly and creative approaches to translation, including some specific strategies and methods. The talk will also offer a broad overview of the contemporary landscape of translated work, with reference to some important recent published books in the literary scene.

REPAIR CAFE RVA

Sunday, November 15th from 1:30 PM – 4:00 PM

Repair Cafe RVA is a place to bring your favorite broken thing. We'll be repairing appliances, bikes, electronics, furniture, jewelry, textiles, toys, and more! Arrive early, as sign up is first-come, first-served. Repair Cafe volunteers will get you signed in and connect you with the right person for your repair! Repair Cafe RVA is a local chapter of an international non-profit organization based in the Netherlands.

YARN YIPPEE!

Wednesday, November 18th from 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM

For individuals working on personal projects to come together, socialize, and learn from each other. Some beginner supplies available, first come first serve. 3

PROTECT YOURSELF FROM FRAUD

Thursday, November 19th from 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM

Please join us for a fraud protection presentation hosted by AARP. The presentation will be geared towards seniors (but all are welcome) and it will review commons scams and fraud attempts online and over the phone. Attendees will learn to spot scams as well as what resources they have if they have fallen victim to fraud. There will be time at the end of the lecture for a Q&A session.

ORAL HISTORY TRAINING WORKSHOP

Saturday, November 21st from 1:00 PM – 2:30 PM

This hands-on workshop introduces participants to the fundamentals of oral history collection and preservation. Attendees will learn interview techniques, ethical considerations, recording best practices, and strategies for preserving family and community stories using accessible tools and technology. Participants will leave with practical skills for documenting local history and preserving personal narratives for future generations.

RICHMOND FREE PRESS LEGACY CELEBRATION

Sunday, November 22nd from 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM

A multi-faceted celebration of the Richmond Free Press’s 34 year run as an independent, Black-owned newspaper focused on local issues and the African-American community in Richmond. The archives of the newspaper and papers of Raymond Boone Sr. (Editor, Co-Founder) were donated to the Richmond Public Library by the Boones in April 2026 to ensure that future generations have access to the valuable historical information they contain. This event will feature a conversation with Jean Patterson Boone, recognition of longtime RFP staff, exhibits/samples from the collection, and an opportunity for people to search for their stories in the RFP.

entry.title: Some observations after 2 months of useful.bike
entry.content:
From useful.bike

Some observations after 2 months of useful.bike

Two months ago I merged this Tumblr and a local cargo bike Instagram into useful.bike. Some observations on the process:

  • I publish first at Tumblr - I like being able to mix words and photos and links, it feels like real writing. I don’t know that anyone actually reads the site here though.
  • It took me a minute to figure out that I needed to push everything to Insta to get read, the whole story as slides not just a headline (like this)
  • The conversation happens at Instagram & that has made a huge difference in finding an audience
  • I’m also on Bluesky because I like it & other places to see what happens

entry.title: UPDATE: Jahnke Road Improvements Project
entry.content:
From useful.bike

Stretching from Blakemore Road to Forest Hill Avenue, the $42 million Jahnke Road Improvements Project will redraw the corridor with 2 11-foot travel lanes with a center median, dedicated left-turn lanes, a new curb-and-gutter drainage system, an 8-foot multi-use path on the north side, and a 5-foot sidewalk on the south side.

In the works since late 2008 with construction underway since February of this year, the project is expected to be completed by spring 2028.

The multi-use path will fill a crucial gap in the Southside’s bike infrastructure and will connect Forest Hill/Semmes/Westover Hills to Hioaks/German School Road/Warwick/Broad Rock.

entry.title: You Are In The Bike Lane Richmond, October 29

author.name: You Are In The Bike Lane Richmond

entry.content:
From You Are In The Bike Lane Richmond



The Mayo Bridge that connects Manchester to Shockoe Bottom is old and crumbling, so the city is building a replacement bridge directly next to the current one. The link to the survey to give your feedback on the proposed design is in my bio, and you have between now and this Sunday, November 1st, to fill it out.

This is our best opportunity yet to finally get real barrier-protected bike lanes on a bridge here in Richmond. Unfortunately, the current proposal only separates cyclists from busy car traffic using 3-inch bumps. These bumps won't stop drivers from illegally parking or driving in the bike lanes. We know unprotected bike lanes cause delays for emergency services and force cyclists to merge into dangerous car traffic to get around cars.

Thankfully, there's an alternative design that's been popping up across the U.S. that uses barrier-protected bike lanes to give emergency services a way to bypass car traffic. These are called Safety Lanes because they've been proven to improve response times for emergency vehicles while also improving safety for cyclists and pedestrians. This model would be easy for VDOT to adopt because guidelines for emergency vehicles using bike lanes already exist in a design guide Richmond and VDOT already reference.

So fill out the Mayo Bridge Public Survey from the link in my bio, say no to the current proposal that uses small mountable bumps, and ask for safety lanes, barrier-protected double-wide bike lanes that meet the community's safety needs while improving emergency response times.

entry.title: Three Notched Trail could one day connect Richmond and Charlottesville
entry.content:
From useful.bike

The proposed Three Notched Trail is envisioned as part of a 200-mile path that will connect across Virginia from the mountains to the sea.

The first 24 mile stretch through western Albemarle County, connecting the City of Charlottesville and the Blue Ridge Tunnel in Nelson County is currently in the “gathering public support” phase - there is no timeline or budget attached.

A future phase could connect east to Richmond and link up with the expanding Virginia Capital Trail and the Fall Line Trail.

entry.title: RVA Commuter Bike Bus, October 28

This morning was the last commuter bike bus of the season! We were going back and forth on this, but ultimately, folks want to get into work when it’s cold, so we’re taking a page from our commuter bike bus friends in Raleigh and going on hiatus during the cold months. We had 13 weeks of bike bus this first season, and got to meet and hang out with lots of different folks on their way to work! entry.title: just brainstorming Mayo Bridge
entry.content:
From r/rva

My understanding from the various designs that balance cars/bikes/pedestrians in many of these situations, not just a major bridge reconstruction, is emergency vehicle transport systems of speed is a key factor/constraint in design. Am I wrong to assume that emergency vehicle transport systems of speed will be affected as the Mayo Bridge is reconstructed? I'm curious how these emergency transport systems function during long-term construction. Definitely not trying to reduce emergency response time, but genuinely concerned if long term master plans of emergency response is a variable in this decades-long project with regards to having a physical barrier between people and giant machines. Basically asking how often fire trucks and ambulances need to go around traffic across rivers in the age of 2030-2040 vs how often people might get hit by a machine while biking, skating or walking across the bridge. The advantage people in cars have is a built-in protection layer. I wish people not in cars had that layer. anD not trying to be a smartass but fire trucks and ambulances can be redesigned to suit the needs of the where people are. We are discussing a bridge for the 2030's.

entry.title: Proposed cycle track on 6th Street from Franklin to Canal
entry.content:
From useful.bike

The City of Richmond Department of Transportation is seeking feedback on a proposed cycle track along 6th Street between Franklin Street and Canal Street.

The cycle track would link up with the Franklin Street Cycle Track and is along the proposed route of the Fall Line Line Trail.

The base deign of the cycle track is a 2-way bike traffic separated from vehicular traffic with a painted box and plastic divider poles.

There are 2 options presented for the stretch from Franklin to Cary. Alternate 1 has the cycle track, 2 lanes of traffic, and 1 lane of parking. Alternate 2 has the cycle track, 1 lane of traffic, and 2 lanes of parking.

The one design for the stretch from Cary Street to Canal Street has the cycle track, 1 lane of traffic in each direction, and 1 lane of parking.

entry.title: Breakaway RVA, October 24
entry.content:
From Breakaway RVA



Tragedies, death and dismemberment are sadly part of history and in a historic city like Richmond there’s no shortage of the horrors which make for a creepy Halloween ride.
Join us Thursday, October 29 to learn some of the horrors of Richmond buried in the history of this city and please keep your eyes open for ghosts haunting these sites. The pace will be easy but we will climb the Franklin/Bank/9th Street hill. Please bring lights and a good blinkie light because much of this haunted ride will be in the dark.
Meeting time and location: 5:45pm at Clark Spring Elementary School (1101 Dance Street, Richmond, VA 23220
Meet at 5:45 and leave at 6:00pm
End Point: Clark Springs Elementary School
